title: Music Promotion Services (2026): How to Hire Safely
description: How to hire music promotion help safely: what real promotion includes, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags that can hurt your music.
intro: Music promotion can help new listeners find your songs through playlist curators, blogs, social media and ads. It is also an area full of risk: some services use bots or fake streams, which can get your music removed and your account penalized by streaming platforms and distributors. Real promotion aims at real listeners and makes no promises about exact numbers. This guide helps you tell the difference.

faq.q: Can I pay for playlist placements?
faq.a: Paying curators directly for guaranteed placement is against the rules of major streaming platforms. Legitimate services pitch your song to curators who decide freely, or run ads that lead real people to your music.

Streams generated by bots or click farms. Streaming platforms detect them, and consequences can include removed streams, withheld royalties or removed releases. Avoid any service that guarantees a number of streams.
Pitching to independent curators, blogs and radio, running targeted ads, social media campaigns and creator collaborations. Results vary and are not guaranteed.
Look at listeners, saves, follows and where streams come from in your artist dashboard. Real promotion usually brings listeners who save songs and return.

faq.q: Do I need anything before promoting?
faq.a: A finished, well-mixed song, cover art, an up-to-date artist profile and clear links. Promotion works best when the music and profile are ready.
